replay.command: bash replay_e16.sh PYTHON ABS_OUTDIR [--board KA|KB] [--through ROUND] [--resume]
replay.KA: Independent replay from tracked sources through t2. Rounds base-r3 reproduce the retained content exactly (comparison: replay/20261013-r4-t2/KA-replay-comparison.json).
replay.KB: Independent replay from tracked sources through t2, run serialized under the host heavy-run guard: every step within 180 s / 2 GiB (longest step 104.8 s, peak RSS 1.39 GiB). Rounds base-r3 reproduce the retained content exactly: per-round counts, prefix-preserved source objects, the full 2,898-object access delta, the r3 graph and physical ports, and the complete 521-identity census (replay/20261013-r4-t2/KB-replay-comparison.json).
replay.comparison_method: compare_replay.py: per-round count and residual-identity equality; each round keeps the previous round's objects as an exact prefix with unique ids; added objects equal the retained r3 delta; final graph and census equal after removing only seal fields (input_sha256, parent_sha256, graph_sha256, elapsed_seconds, peak_KiB). Clipped sheets and caps are not retained as files, so their geometry is compared only through graph/census equality.
replay.original_execution_receipts: The 2026-10-12 base-r3 receipts (K?-{base,r1,r2,r3}-*-execution.json) are kept unchanged as the original execution record; the new run is a separate replay, not a replacement.
replay.seal_note: Execution receipts seal absolute input paths and the method bytes in use; byte hashes are therefore run-local. Content comparison excludes those seal fields.
replay.resume: replay_steps.py writes steps/<step>.json binding input, method and output SHA-256. --resume reuses a step only when all three still match; stale, partial or failed outputs are moved to rejected/ and the step and its dependents rerun. The step ledgers of this run are in replay/20261013-r4-t2/.
replay.resume_observed: KB r2/r3 were rejected as stale after construct_access.py was briefly edited and restored to its retained bytes (8b1ded18...); the rebuilt KB r2 source was byte-identical, so its evaluation was hash-reused. t1/t2 on both boards were rejected after two_face.py gained the shared-bore refusal; the rebuilt t2 sources were byte-identical (KA 9e9f6708..., KB 368d3def...). Defect found by review and fixed: the earlier rejection moved the step ledger under the same name as its <step>.json output, replacing the moved stale KB r2/r3 sources. Their SHA-256 values survive in those ledgers and equal the rebuilt files, so no content was lost; ledgers are now kept as ledger-<step>.json (test_replay_steps). Receipts: replay/20261013-r4-t2/rejected/.
replay.scope: base-r3 were executed on 2026-10-12 and independently replayed here; r4, t1 and t2 have one execution each (this run), so they are reproducible from tracked files but not yet independently replayed.

representative_direct_load.obstruction: every 0.6 mm via site within 2 mm blocked by U1105/U1107 face pads and signal vias; straight path to feed-connected pin 9 crosses no-connect pin 10
representative_direct_load.target: U1107 pin 9 (AGND), feed-connected via its own r1 access via
representative_direct_load.bounds: route window 6x6 mm at 0.05 mm pitch; each step under 180 s / 2 GiB

method_note: Rounds r1/r2 were produced while construct_access.py was still gaining the r3 options; the KA replay with the final method reproduced r1-r3 content exactly.

replay_history.KA: unguarded replay from tracked sources reproduced the content of every KA artifact (normalized, sheets, r1-r3 sources, final graph/census); file hashes differ only through path-bound seal metadata
replay_history.KB: normalized board content reproduced; KB access-round replay NOT RUN (clip step exceeded 180 s under machine load; the guarded rerun was stopped by the host for low memory)

round_decisions.r4: construct_access.py --method route with r3 planes, graph and census, unchanged method bytes. r4 closed KA 8 / KB 10. A further same-method round would only gain these 18 closures as new targets, so no r5 was run.
round_decisions.t1: two_face.py --use-fed-transitions on one representative direct-load IC pin per board (evidence/e16/t1-batch.json), then the full census.
round_decisions.t2: The same mechanism on every remaining residual, as one bounded batch per board (13-15 s construction).

finite_network.producer: bash run_finite_network.sh PYTHON RUNDIR t2 ABS_OUTDIR; python summarize_network.py --runs ABS_OUTDIR --round t2 --output finite-network-t2.json
finite_network.status: CONDITIONAL_PARTIAL_MODEL_NETWORK; NOT A BOUND; NOT ELECTRICAL COMPLIANCE
finite_network.resources: 34 runs, each within 180 s / 2 GiB; see run_files_sha256 in finite-network-t2.json
finite_network.rerun: Rerun after review: barrels attach only to the sheet piece containing their centre, and the drop figure is null when any port lacks a finite path. Port resistances were unchanged.
